title: Suffering close: the wounds that shine
hook: the risen Christ still bears his wounds, now glorious
tomorrow: five years in. what will you actually keep doing?

segments.voice: Yesterday's line: hope confoundeth not, a promise-keeper instead of the odds. Today this whole block on suffering ends, on the evening of the first Easter.
screen: `HOPE CONFOUNDETH NOT.` → `THE BLOCK ENDS ON EASTER EVENING.`

segments.voice: Everybody has a scar story. The bike, the kitchen knife, the surgery. People roll up a sleeve to tell it. John tells one too. It's the evening of the first Easter, and the doors are shut, John says, for fear. The disciples have heard rumors all day and seen nothing. Then Jesus is standing in the middle of the room, saying, "Peace be to you." And before anything else, he does something odd.
screen: `EVERYBODY HAS A SCAR STORY.` → `THE DOORS ARE SHUT.` → `PEACE BE TO YOU.`

segments.voice: John says, in the Douay-Rheims: "he shewed them his hands and his side. The disciples therefore were glad, when they saw the Lord." The wounds come first. Not a speech. Here's one to tell a friend: Thomas gets remembered for the wounds, but he wasn't in the room. The others saw them a week before he did. Why keep them? A risen body could surely be flawless. But the wounds are how his friends know it's him, the same one who died, not a stand-in. Notice what the wounds don't do: they don't accuse. He shows them to the friends who ran away, and his first word is peace. And they've changed. The Apocalypse sees "a Lamb standing as it were slain": wounded, and standing. Isaiah had said it: "by his bruises we are healed." Saint Thomas Aquinas taught that the risen wounds remain for glory. They don't hurt now. They shine, the way a story shines once it has ended well. That's the close of this block. It began with being ill and in pain, walked through doubt, grief and dying, and ends here: not wounds erased, but wounds that shine. Next comes the last climb.
screen: `HIS HANDS AND HIS SIDE.` · `THOMAS WASN'T THERE YET.` · `A LAMB STANDING, AS IF SLAIN.` · `THE BLOCK ENDS HERE.` · then, large: `WOUNDS THAT SHINE.`

segments.voice: Turn your palms up on your lap. Bring to mind one wound you carry, old or new, in body or heart. Don't explain it or fix it; just hold it open, the way he held out his hands. If you pray, you can offer it to him as it is.
Suffering close. The block ends on the risen Christ, still wounded, and the wounds now shine.
Pocket this one: wounds that shine, kept so his friends would know him. Day 1730, done.

screen: `DAY 1730 COUNTS.` → `TOMORROW: FIVE YEARS IN. WHAT WILL YOU ACTUALLY KEEP DOING?`

chat.meaning: The risen Christ showed his hands and side first. His wounds weren't erased; they became how his friends knew him.
